function_1: legitimate pollinator visitation and seed production
eligibility_reason: Short-tubed flowers experience lower robbery, higher legitimate visitation and higher seed production in the presence of robbers; when robbers are excluded, tube-length differences in pollination and seed production disappear.
source_basis: Tie et al. 2023 Plant Diversity DOI 10.1016/j.pld.2022.11.002
notes: Realized routes both favor shorter tubes under robbery, but legitimate-visitor effects are antagonist-context dependent and visitor roles can switch.

eligibility_reason: Nectar volume covaries with tube length and robber-intensity groups, but the source does not isolate two independent fitness components for nectar volume itself.
source_basis: Tie et al. 2023 Plant Diversity DOI 10.1016/j.pld.2022.11.002
notes: Retained without inheriting the corolla-tube result.

eligibility_reason: Sugar concentration varies among robber-intensity groups and with floral phenotype, but a trait-specific two-route fitness geometry is not isolated.
source_basis: Tie et al. 2023 Plant Diversity DOI 10.1016/j.pld.2022.11.002

eligibility_reason: Longer corolla tubes receive more robbing, while the source does not identify a matched tube-length effect on plant reproductive success; many pollinating bee species also rob.
source_basis: Layek et al. 2024 PLOS ONE DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0300398
notes: Robbing frequency changes across flowering period and time of day, but robbing does not significantly change fruit or seed set.

eligibility_reason: Higher nectar availability increases visitor abundance and strongly reduces the fraction of robbing visits, but the manipulation is not linked to an independent antagonist fitness cost.
source_basis: Layek et al. 2024 PLOS ONE DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0300398
notes: Resource availability changes visitor tactics rather than yielding a fixed pollinator-versus-antagonist geometry.

eligibility_reason: Herbivores weaken selection for increased inflorescence production, whereas pollinators show no independent selection effect on this trait.
source_basis: Santangelo et al. 2019 Journal of Evolutionary Biology DOI 10.1111/jeb.13392
notes: A clear one-sided/null geometry on a common reproductive-fitness analysis.

eligibility_reason: Herbivores weaken selection on flower size among acyanogenic plants, while pollinators show no independent effect on flower-size selection.
source_basis: Santangelo et al. 2019 Journal of Evolutionary Biology DOI 10.1111/jeb.13392
notes: One-sided/null geometry is itself defence-genotype dependent.

eligibility_reason: Pollinators weaken selection for later flowering among cyanogenic plants but not acyanogenic plants; the optimized source model does not retain an independent herbivore-mediated flowering-time effect.
source_basis: Santangelo et al. 2019 Journal of Evolutionary Biology DOI 10.1111/jeb.13392; full-text results and model table
notes: One-sided/null geometry with defence-genotype context dependence: pollinator-mediated phenology selection is conditional, while an independent herbivore-mediated phenology component is not supported.

eligibility_reason: Flower size is positively associated with robbing frequency in one population, but a matched pollinator-mediated effect of flower size is not source-resolved.
source_basis: Castro et al. 2009 Ecological Research DOI 10.1007/s11284-008-0481-5
notes: Do not promote the paper-level proposed robber-mediated negative selection to a two-route conflict without matched pollinator direction.

eligibility_reason: Legitimate pollination is primarily influenced by nectar reward, while a matched robber preference/effect for the nectar-reward axis is not frozen.
source_basis: Castro et al. 2009 Ecological Research DOI 10.1007/s11284-008-0481-5
notes: Negative correlations between robbing frequency and legitimate pollination in two populations are not treated as trait-specific opposing components.
